statement: Two independent generations report the same doubt about reg-report-bare-noun-compression and reg-report-hedge-language: both were derived from macro-forecast writing (KDI, KIET, KCMI) and both sit less naturally outside it. On the housing supply-pipeline analysis the bare-noun compression was usable but not idiomatic, and the hedge vocabulary fit partly because Korean housing-statistics commentary already borrows the macro register — not demonstrably because the rule is domain-general. On the tools topic, which analyses an argument rather than forecasting anything, the compression device had only one honest place to go. Neither rule is wrong; both may be scoped wider than their evidence reaches. The two report rules are currently generality genre_local over research/academic, which asserts the whole genre. The corpus behind them is three economics institutions. Recorded at task_local scope: this is an agent observation, and basis "model_inference" may not carry scope "calibration_candidate" on its own — agent consensus never silently becomes durable preference. Promoting this finding into the pack requires the owner.

routing.rationale: This is a scope question about two GENRE_CONVENTION rules — whether a report-register device observed in macro-economics writing holds across the research/academic content type — which is the register layer's own concern. Deliberately not routed to native_fluency: the prose these rules produced is not unidiomatic, it is idiomatic for a register that may not be the right one for the piece. Confidence is medium because two agent generations agreeing is weaker evidence than two institutions, and neither is a Korean reader's judgement.
